title: Trains to Swindon
from: the main stations in the south, west and Midlands
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Royal International Air Tattoo. RAF Fairford has no station of its own, so the plan is a train to Swindon, then the free Swindon Shuttle bus to the Yellow entry. GWR runs trains into Swindon every few minutes from London and Reading, and often from Bristol, Bath, Oxford and Cardiff too. There are three ways in by train and bus, so pick the one that suits you above. Then pick your station, a day and a time below and I’ll work out the shuttle you’re likely to get as well.
facts: Every day, shuttles Friday to Sunday
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for RIAT. From here it’s a short walk to the bus station and the shuttle to the airfield. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: Out of the station it’s about a 5 minute walk to the Swindon Bus Interchange on Fleming Way, where the free Swindon Shuttle leaves from Stop N. It takes about 30 minutes and drops you at the Yellow entry, at the eastern end of the showground. You do need to pre-book it, by picking the ticket with the Swindon Shuttle Bus when you buy your RIAT tickets.
walkBack: The shuttles back leave from the Yellow entry. Leave plenty of time to walk there across the showground, as it’s a big site, and expect a queue at the busy times.
offTag: Change here for the shuttle bus
note: Train times are from the National Rail timetable for Thursday 5 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Monday to Wednesday use the Thursday times), checked on 30 October 2026, so they are a guide to how trains run on those days of the week rather than the show weekend times. The shuttle times are the latest ones published for RIAT and may change for 2027. Times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, so please check before you travel. The railway and the bus route are drawn along the lines and roads, so treat them as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: Trains to Swindon, then the free Swindon Shuttle. Most trains into Swindon are GWR, with CrossCountry and South Western Railway helping from Birmingham and the south coast. I’ve only included the big stations where the whole trip works. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there.

bus.name: Swindon Shuttle
bus.title: The Swindon Shuttle
bus.intro: The last bit is by bus. I’ve worked out the shuttle you’re likely to catch for the train you picked, so you can see when you’ll actually be at the gate.
bus.queue: The shuttles work on a first come, first served basis, so on a busy morning you may not get the first one that leaves. I would add a bit of time.
bus.tip: The shuttle needs pre-booking with your RIAT ticket, and it’s free. Exit queues for the shuttles back can be slow, so I would buy a flexible train ticket home rather than an Advance ticket tied to one train.
notes: The Swindon Shuttle is free, but you have to pre-book it. When you buy your RIAT tickets, choose the ticket that includes the Swindon Shuttle Bus.
If you pick the shuttle, you can’t bring a car to the show as well. There’s pay and display parking in Swindon town centre if you’re driving to the station.
These are the latest shuttle times RIAT has put out, so they may change for 2027. On the Friday the last shuttle back leaves at 18:00, and on the Saturday and Sunday at 19:30.
Kemble is closer on the map, but there’s no RIAT shuttle from there, so I would stick with Swindon.
bus.queueBack: Everyone heads for the shuttles once the flying finishes, so the queue at the Yellow entry can be long. I would get there early, or stay for the later buses when it’s quieter.
bus.offDay: check what’s on at RAF Fairford before you travel, and book a taxi from Swindon, as the shuttles are only laid on for the show days

about.Reading|Didcot Parkway: Along the Thames valley through Goring Gap.
about.Didcot Parkway|Swindon: Along the Vale of the White Horse. Keep an eye out on the left for the White Horse at Uffington on the hillside.
about.Reading|Swindon: Along the Thames valley and the Vale of the White Horse. Look out on the left for the Uffington White Horse on the hillside.
about.London Paddington|Swindon: Along Brunel’s Great Western through Reading, Didcot and the Vale of the White Horse.
about.Oxford|Didcot Parkway: South along the Thames through Radley and Culham.
about.Bristol Temple Meads|Bath Spa: Along the Avon valley through Keynsham.
about.Bath Spa|Chippenham: Through Box Tunnel, Brunel’s famous tunnel under Box Hill.
about.Chippenham|Swindon: Across north Wiltshire, past Wootton Bassett.
about.Bath Spa|Swindon: Through Box Tunnel and across north Wiltshire.
about.Bristol Parkway|Swindon: Across south Gloucestershire and through the Chipping Sodbury tunnel.
about.Bristol Temple Meads|Bristol Parkway: Through Bristol’s northern suburbs, past Filton, home of Aerospace Bristol and Concorde.
about.Cardiff Central|Newport: A short run along the Gwent Levels.
about.Newport|Bristol Parkway: Under the River Severn through the Severn Tunnel, over four miles long.
about.Cheltenham Spa|Gloucester: A short hop with the Cotswolds off to the east.

about.Gloucester|Kemble: Up the Golden Valley through Stroud and the Sapperton tunnel.
about.Kemble|Swindon: Down past Kemble, the station nearest RAF Fairford, and into Swindon.
about.Birmingham New Street|Cheltenham Spa: Down the Lickey Incline, the steepest main line in Britain.
about.Southampton Central|Basingstoke: Up through Winchester and over the Hampshire downs.
about.Exeter St Davids|Bristol Temple Meads: Through Tiverton, Taunton and Bridgwater, along the Somerset Levels.
